Josie’s narration conveys distinct perspectives: her own tension between performing maturity and needing support, her father’s determination to preserve joy and dignity, her mother’s protective concern, and Eli’s understated empathy. Although no character is clearly unlikeable, her father’s expectation that Josie fit into his social world and her resulting caregiving role complicate his warmth. These tensions make the characters believable rather than idealized.
